flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d4 with your e-pawn is the strongest move because you take the defender of the white c3-knight.
flags.critique: The d4 pawn does not defend the knight on c3. Pawns don't protect backwards. This is the Scotch recapture — I take the pawn that just challenged e5 — and you told me a tactic that isn't on the board. If the removed-defender detector fired because c3 'became hanging' after my pawn landed on d4, that's a geometry bug, not a lesson.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d4 with your f3-knight is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: Nc6 defends d4. This is a recapture, not picking up a loose pawn. Calling it undefended and tagging wins_material teaches me the wrong word for 'take back.' If SEE is positive because the extra pawn sits there, say we recapture — don't pretend Black left it hanging.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: No because, empty reasons, and you still called it strongest while dropping 40cp. In the Four Knights Scotch I'd rather hear that this is a bit cramped compared with ...Bb4, or that it blunts e5 and frees the bishop. 'That's the one.' with a blank stare is not coaching.

flags.quote: Moving your f8-bishop to e7 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: White just pinned my knight to the queen with Bg5. Be7 is how you break a pin. You had 'development' in the reasons and then dropped it as tautology, so I get silence. Teach the unpin — that's the whole point of the move.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on c6 with your d4-knight is the strongest move because you fork the black queen and the black e7-bishop and it unveils an attack from your queen on the black pawn.
flags.critique: A knight that lands on c6 does attack queen and bishop, and then I recapture it next move. That is not a fork I can cash. The real Scotch idea is doubling my c-pawns and maybe looking at d6. Don't lead with a tactic whose piece is hanging.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on c6 with your b-pawn is the strongest move because the knight was undefended.
flags.critique: Yes I recapture a hanging knight — that's table stakes, not 'winning material.' Then you stuffed doubled_pawns and isolated_pawn into the reason list like they're why the move is strong. Those are the scars of the recapture, not a brag.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to f3 is playable, but moving your g5-bishop to e3 would be better.
flags.critique: f3 is the first real inaccuracy and you gave me a better SAN with zero idea. f3 pokes a hole around my king and makes a dark-square mess; Be3 is a normal retreat/developing move that doesn't wreck the shield. 'There's better.' is not a lesson.

flags.quote: Moving your c8-bishop to b7 is playable, but moving your pawn to d5 would be better.
flags.critique: Same empty contrast. ...d5 is the break that fights for the center and hits e4; Bb7 tucks the bishop behind doubled c-pawns. Tell me that, or I'm just memorizing a move I won't find next game.

flags.quote: Moving your e2-bishop to c4 is the strongest move because you pin the pawn to the king.
flags.critique: You mean the f7 pawn can't step off the a2–g8 diagonal without walking into check. That's a legal pin and a useless sentence. The idea of Bc4 is aiming at f7 / the king, and you still called it strongest while bleeding 47cp. Don't teach 'pin the pawn' like I just won something.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d5 is the strongest move because it gives your king better protection.
flags.critique: d5 is a central break that hits the bishop on c4. It does not tuck my king in. If your kingSafer flag fired because the pawn blocks Bc4's diagonal to g8, that's a side effect — lead with the break, not a king-safety phrase-bank line that makes me think I was defending.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d5 with your knight is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended and it unveils an attack from your bishop on the white g5-bishop.
flags.critique: The discovered hit on Bg5 is the actual lesson — keep that. The pawn is not undefended: Nc3 and Bc4 both cover d5. You glued a recapture lie onto a real tactic and I now don't know which half to trust.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on e7 with your g5-bishop is the strongest move because you take the defender of the black queen.
flags.critique: I am not winning the queen. Bg5 was hanging to the discovered Be7, so this is a bishop trade. 'Removed defender of the queen' is detector poetry. Say we trade off the hanging bishop.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on e7 with your e8-rook keeps the position even because the bishop was undefended. A better move would have been taking the bishop on e7 with your queen because you can likely take a knight.
flags.critique: Eval went from -40 to +46 and you called that even. I recaptured a bishop that just took mine — of course it was 'undefended.' Qxe7 does not take a knight on this move; that 'likely' capture is a PV ghost. Teach recapture-with-queen vs recapture-with-rook (activity, the e-file) instead of inventing material.

flags.quote: Taking the queen on d8 with your queen is the strongest move because you fork the black a8-rook and the black king and you take the defender of the black e7-rook.
flags.critique: My queen was hanging to the discovered ...Qd8 and the Ne3 fork. I trade queens with check. I do not fork rook and king in any way that nets a rook, and I do not win the e7 rook by 'removing its defender.' You buried the real story — answer the threat — under two fake tactics.

flags.quote: Taking the queen on d8 with your a8-rook is the strongest move because the queen was undefended.
flags.critique: The rook I just recaptured with is the defender. wins_material on a forced recapture after Qxd8+ is the same lie as ply 9. Stop saying undefended when the piece is sitting on a defended square.

flags.quote: Moving your d8-rook to e8 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: I doubled on the open e-file. That's a textbook rook lesson and you printed a period. Empty reasons, same quip. I can see the file — tell me I'm stacking on it.

flags.quote: Moving your king to f2 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Endgame, queens off, king walks up. That's king activity, and your reasons are king_more_exposed plus pawn_shield — opposite stories, neither in the sentence. Don't treat a centralized king like I blundered my shelter.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on d3 with your knight is the strongest move because you fork the white knight and the white king.
flags.critique: Check, and the knight on c5 is also attacked — then White recaptures with that same knight. The 'fork' never wins the knight. I took a bishop with check. Say that.

flags.quote: Moving your king to e3 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: This is the whole endgame plan starting: king toward the queenside pawns. pawn_shield as the reason is a joke. If you can't name king activity, at least don't call the winning walk 'strongest' with a shrug.

flags.quote: Moving your bishop to f1 is a mistake, but moving your king to e7 would be better.
flags.critique: 136cp dumped and I still don't know why. The bishop goes hunting a knight while White's king runs to d4–c5 to eat c-pawns. Ke7 is 'bring the king' — the same lesson you refused to teach on the last move. 'That was shaky.' without the race is just a vibe.

flags.quote: Moving your king to c5 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: The king is attacking c6 and c7. This is the payoff of the march, and you tagged king_more_exposed like I wandered into mate. A 1200 needs 'king attacks the weak doubled pawns,' not another blank strongest.

flags.quote: Moving your bishop to d3 is a mistake, but moving your bishop to f3 would be better.
flags.critique: Lichess called it an inaccuracy; you upgraded to mistake and still gave no idea. Bf3 hits pawns / stays useful; Bd3 lets the knight into d4. Don't spend the severity budget if you won't spend a because-clause.

flags.quote: Moving your knight to d4 is a mistake, but moving your knight to b4 would be better.
flags.critique: You had saves_piece and outpost in the reasons and used neither. 129cp of advantage evaporated. Nb4 hits a6/c6; Nd4 looks pretty and isn't the squeeze. Same empty 'but' as every other miss.

flags.quote: Moving your bishop to b1 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: ignored_threat is sitting in the reasons and the sentence doesn't mention a2. The bishop goes to the corner to eat a pawn. If you detected the threat, print it.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to g5 is a blunder, but moving your king to c8 would be better because it keeps your king safer.
flags.critique: I hung the g-pawn. White takes it next move. King safer / Kc8 is the wrong movie — this is a pawn blunder in a knight-vs-bishop ending, not a mating-net dodge. Lichess said mistake; you said blunder; neither matters if you teach the wrong threat.

suggestions.title: Reserve 'undefended' for zero defenders
suggestions.detail: wins_material currently says 'the piece was undefended' whenever capturedSeeCp >= pieceValue - 50. Recaptures (Nxd4, bxc6, Rxd8, Nxd3, Rxe7) all pass that bar while the square still has a defender, so a 1200 learns the word wrong. Gate the undefended phrase on defender-count === 0 before the capture; if SEE is only recovering last ply's capture, prefer a recapture reason instead of wins_material.

suggestions.title: Require the captured unit actually defended
suggestions.detail: detectRemovedDefender returns a hit when the captured piece wasn't a defender, as long as the newly hanging unit had exactly one defender (`!wasSole && defendersBefore.length !== 1`). That is how exd4 became 'take the defender of the c3-knight.' Require wasSole, and don't surface removed_defender on equal trades (Bxe7 vs queen, Rxe7 vs the other rook) unless the newly hanging piece is actually winning.

suggestions.title: Don't lecture forks that recapture next ply
suggestions.detail: Nxc6 'forks' queen and bishop, Qxd8+ 'forks' rook and king, Nxd3+ 'forks' king and knight — all recaptured immediately. Fork/discovered_attack should not lead if the landing piece's SEE is <= 0 or the forked unit is the recapturer. A 1200 will chase ghosts. Keep geometric forks that net material or force a concession.

suggestions.title: Stop inventing 'you can likely take a knight'
suggestions.detail: Suggested-move benefits pull later PV captures as likely:true. Rxe7's improvement Qxe7 then claimed a knight that isn't taken on that move. verifyLikelyTactics already drops likely tactics on tiny eval swings; also require the capture to be ply-1 of the improvement, or a forced recapture, before move-copy is allowed to say 'you can likely take X.' Vague piece names without squares make it worse.

suggestions.title: Teach king marches as activity, not exposure
suggestions.detail: Kf2, Ke3, Kd4, Kc5 are the winning plan (king to the weak c-pawns) and copy is blank while king_more_exposed / pawn_shield fire with the wrong polarity. Add a king_activity benefit when phase is endgame and the king steps toward center or enemy pawns; suppress king_more_exposed as a benefit of a classified-best king move. Same gap on Bf1 vs Ke7: the mistake is leaving the race, not a nameless SAN swap.

suggestions.title: Don't emit 'strongest move' with no because
suggestions.detail: dropTautologyReasons strips development whenever the moved piece matches, so Be7, Be2, d6, Rde8, Ba6, and a dozen endgame plies render as a period. If benefits are empty, fall back to a plan slot: unpin (detect the Bg5 pin break), double on an open file, develop toward castling, king activity. Silence plus 'That's the one.' is the aesthetic failure of this dump.

suggestions.title: Don't call an 86cp swing 'even'
suggestions.detail: classifyEvalFrame 'holds' if both before and after are inside ±50, ignoring the swing. Rxe7 is -40 → +46, classified inaccuracy, verdict 'keeps the position even.' If classification is inaccuracy/mistake/blunder, skip the holds verdict; or require the delta to be small, not just both numbers near zero. A 1200 hears 'even' and stops looking for the better recapture.

suggestions.title: Always say why the better move is better
suggestions.detail: f3, Bb7, Bf1, a6, Bd3, Nd4, g5 all contrast a SAN with an empty suggestedBecause. Templates already support 'would be better because …' — the gap is contrastBenefits leaving nothing teachable. Prefer one concrete suggested reason: king-safety hole (f3), central break (d5), hung pawn (g5/fxg5), defend c6 (Be4 already worked on ply 64). Wrong because (Kc8 'keeps king safer' on a hung g-pawn) is worse than none, so rank pawn-hanging above king_safer when the eval spike is a captured pawn.

whatWorked: ...Nc6 as saving e5 from Nf3 is the right beginner lesson.
Bg5 'you pin the knight to the queen' is clean and true.
Castling copy (king tucks, rook comes in) actually teaches the move.
exd5 saving the c4-bishop from ...d5 is the right capture story.
...Nxd5 unveiling Be7 onto Bg5 is a real discovered-attack lesson (buried under 'undefended').
...Kd7 saving c6 from Kc5, and a3 saving a2 from ...Bb1, are concrete endgame saves.
Ply 64 naming the hanging c-pawn to king and knight, with ...Be4 as the save, is the coaching this game needed more of.
